points.description: Asynchronous transmission: each character is sent as a self-contained unit framed by a start bit and a stop bit.
points.partial_credit: Only one of start bit / stop bit mentioned, or self-contained character unit without start/stop bits.

points.description: Asynchronous transmission is simple/cheap but gives low transmission rates.
points.partial_credit: Only one of simple/cheap or low rate stated.

points.description: Synchronous transmission: several characters are pooled into a continuous stream of data (frames), with frames delimited by SYN characters or flags.
points.partial_credit: Continuous stream/frames of many characters stated but delimiting by SYN/flag missing (or the reverse).

points.description: Synchronous transmission has higher complexity but higher transmission rates, and requires synchronization between sender and receiver.
points.partial_credit: Two of the three (higher complexity, higher rate, sender-receiver synchronization) stated.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both modes described with the specific features: start/stop bit per character versus frames of pooled characters delimited by SYN/flag, plus the trade-offs (cost/rate/complexity/synchronization). Generic statements like "async is slower" without the stated detail earn nothing for that point. Any wrong detail (e.g. start/stop bits attributed to synchronous mode) cancels that point.
